statement_utf8:
Let $q$ be a prime power, and let $[n,k_1,d_1]_q$ and $[n,k_2,d_2]_q$ denote $q$-ary linear codes of length $n$, dimensions $k_1,k_2$, and minimum distances $d_1,d_2$. Two codes form a **linear $\ell$-intersection pair** when the dimension of their intersection is $\ell$.

**Guenda et al.'s conjecture.** Provided that $[n,k_1,d_1]_q$ and $[n,k_2,d_2]_q$ codes exist, there exists a linear $\ell$-intersection pair of such codes for every integer $\ell$ satisfying

$$
k_1+k_2-n\leq \ell\leq \min\{k_1,k_2\}.
$$

The lower bound is forced by the dimension formula for the intersection of two length-$n$ codes, while the upper bound is immediate from the two dimensions. The conjecture asks whether every admissible intersection dimension can always be realized while preserving the specified code parameters; the supplied text does not report a resolution.

title: Guenda et al.'s conjecture on linear intersection pairs of codes

statement_utf8:
Let $M$ be an $n\times m$ $t$-disjunct matrix with constant column weight $b$. Set

$$
p=\frac{b+t-1}{t},
$$

and assume that $p$ is an integer. A Steiner system $\mathfrak{S}(n,b,p)$ is a family of $b$-subsets of an $n$-element set such that every $p$-subset is contained in exactly one member; the maximum such family is denoted by $\mathfrak{S}(n,b,p)$. **Steiner-system conjecture.** The maximum $\mathfrak{S}(n,b,p)$ Steiner system gives a matrix $M'$ that is no worse than $M$, equivalently,

$$
|\mathfrak{S}(n,b,p)|\ge m.
$$

The conjecture proposes that Steiner-system constructions are at least as efficient as arbitrary constant-column-weight $t$-disjunct matrices with the same parameters. The surrounding discussion notes that the Steiner construction yields a $\left\lfloor\frac{b-1}{p-1}\right\rfloor$-disjunct matrix, but the supplied text gives no resolution of this conjecture.
technical_review: An exact Steiner system requires divisibility/existence, while a maximum packing is a different object; literal text uses the same symbol for both. A divisibility counterexample would be a wording correction. Need primary definitions before any set-system enumeration.
title: Steiner-system extremal conjecture for constant-column-weight disjunct matrices

statement_utf8:
Let $SPT_*$ be the simplicial group of simplicial pure twin groups, let $c_{111}$ be the 2-simplex with trivial faces, and let $K_*$ be the smallest simplicial subgroup of $SPT_*$ containing $c_{111}$. Let $S^2$ be the simplicial sphere with non-degenerate 2-simplex $\sigma=(0,1,2)$, and let $F[S^2]_*$ be Milnor's free simplicial group on $S^2$. The simplicial homomorphism

$$
\Theta:F[S^2]_*\longrightarrow K_*
$$

is induced by the simplicial map sending $\sigma$ to $c_{111}$. **The simplicial freeness conjecture.** The homomorphism

$$
\Theta:F[S^2]_*\longrightarrow K_*
$$

is an isomorphism. This would identify the simplicial subgroup generated by $c_{111}$ with Milnor's free simplicial group on the simplicial 2-sphere, extending the verified injectivity in degrees at most $4$ and providing a description of the homotopy groups of $S^3$ through the Moore complex of $K_*$.
technical_review: Pure twin simplicial operators and c111 are not defined literally. Surjectivity is generated by construction; injectivity beyond degree4 is the substance. Low-degree checks give no full-scope route to all degrees.
title: The simplicial freeness conjecture for the Brunnian planar braid subgroup

statement_utf8:
Let $E_{\alpha,\beta}$ denote the Mittag–Leffler function. There exists some $\alpha_0\in(1.59911,1.59912)$, and for $\alpha\geq\alpha_0$ let $Z_2(\alpha)$ denote the smallest positive solution of $E_{\alpha,2}(-z^\alpha)=0$.

**Smallest-zero conjecture for $E_{\alpha,2}$.** For each $\alpha\in[\alpha_0,2]$, the equation

$$
E_{\alpha,2}(-z^\alpha)=0
$$

has at least one solution in $(0,\infty)$. As $\alpha\to2-$,

$$
Z_2(\alpha)=\pi+(2-\alpha)+o(2-\alpha),
$$

and as $\alpha\to\alpha_0+$,

$$
Z_2(\alpha)=Z_2(\alpha_0)+c(\alpha-\alpha_0)^b(1+o(1)),
$$

where $Z_2(\alpha_0)\approx5.21066$, $b\approx1/2$, and $c\approx-4.8$. Furthermore, $Z_2(\alpha)$ is strictly decreasing in $\alpha$. For each $\alpha\in(1,\alpha_0)$, $E_{\alpha,2}(-z^\alpha)>0$ for all $z\geq0$.

The threshold and the asserted behavior are based on numerical observations; the exact value of $\alpha_0$ and the stated asymptotics and monotonicity remain unproved here. The context attributes the existence of a threshold to earlier work but does not establish these precise claims.
technical_review: Approximate b and c are not exact asserted constants. Local implicit-function expansion near2 cannot settle global monotonicity or exclude extra zeros below threshold. Rigorous zero isolation and a global sign mechanism are missing; no numerical sweep.
title: Conjecture on the zeros of the Mittag–Leffler function with second parameter 2

statement_utf8:
Let $\mathcal{S}^d$ denote the space of $d$-dimensional shifts, and let the **Cantor–Bendixson rank** and **Cantor–Bendixson residue** refer to the usual transfinite derivative rank and its stable remainder. A shift has **maximality type infinity** if its maximality type is infinite; a shift of finite type is a shift defined by finitely many forbidden patterns, and a minimal subsystem is a subsystem minimal under inclusion.

**Cantor–Bendixson structure conjecture.** For all $d>1$, the Cantor–Bendixson rank of $\mathcal{S}^d$ is $\omega$. Furthermore, the Cantor–Bendixson residue is the closure of the set of shifts having maximality type infinity. The shifts which are not in this residue are precisely those that can be written as a finite union of shifts of finite type which are the limit of their minimal subsystems.

The preceding results show that shifts of maximality type infinity lie in the Cantor–Bendixson residue and that this set has empty interior, but they do not determine the full residue or the rank. The conjecture proposes a complete description of both the rank and the shifts outside the residue.
technical_review: Maximality type infinity is circularly named, and topology/alphabet conventions are absent. Showing one inclusion already mentioned in the statement leaves converse and transfinite rank untouched; no small full-scope certificate.
title: Conjecture on the Cantor–Bendixson structure of spaces of shifts

quantifier_scope_review: Completeness of minimum quasigroup generation under the intended reduction class, with at most log n generators.
source_body_coverage: No primary body read; literal corpus statement screening only
statement_utf8:
A **quasigroup** is an algebra whose multiplication table is a Latin square; equivalently, for all elements $a,b$, there are unique elements $x,y$ such that $ax=b$ and $ya=b$. The **minimum generating set problem** asks whether a given quasigroup has a generating set of size at most $\log n$, where $n$ is the order of the quasigroup.

**Papadimitriou–Yannakakis' conjecture.** The minimum generating set problem for quasigroups is $\exists^{\log^2 n}\mathsf{P}$-complete.

Papadimitriou and Yannakakis established the analogous completeness result for arbitrary magmas and conjectured that completeness persists for the more structured class of quasigroups. The paper reports an unconditional refutation of a version of this conjecture for completeness under quasi-polynomial-size constant-depth reductions, and a refutation under polylogarithmic-space reductions assuming $\mathsf{EXP}\neq\mathsf{PSPACE}$, so the conjecture is treated as refuted.
technical_review: Statement and references conflict on refutation; completeness depends on reduction model, log rounding and whether division operations enter generation. Conditional non-completeness for one reduction class cannot be promoted to an unconditional full refutation. Primary body unread.
title: Papadimitriou–Yannakakis' completeness conjecture for minimum generating sets of quasigroups

quantifier_scope_review: Under the three determinacy/inner-model assumptions and each successor Solovay zeta satisfying the HOD_X equality, the specified V_zeta models ZF plus the club HOD-Berkeley assertion.

statement_utf8:
Assume

$$
{\sf{AD}}_{\mathbb{R}}+V=L(\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}))+“\Theta\text{ is a regular cardinal}”.
$$

Let $\Theta$ be the least ordinal not surjected by a real. Suppose $\zeta<\Theta$ is a successor member of the Solovay sequence, let $\nu$ be the largest member of the Solovay sequence below $\zeta$, set

$$
X=\bigcup_{\alpha<\zeta}\alpha^\omega,
$$

and let

$$
\Delta=\{A\subseteq\mathbb{R}:\text{the Wadge rank of }A\text{ is }<\nu\}.
$$

Assume also that $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R})\cap{\sf{HOD}}_X=\Delta$. A cardinal $\kappa$ is a **club $N$-Berkeley cardinal** if for every $M\in N$ there is a club $C\subseteq\kappa$ such that for every $\alpha\in C$ there is an elementary embedding $j:M\to M$ with $\operatorname{crit}(j)=\alpha$.

**Solovay-sequence conjecture.** Under these assumptions, $V_\zeta^{{\sf{HOD}}_X}$ is a model of

$$
{\sf{ZF}+“\omega_1\text{ is a club }{\sf{HOD}}\text{-Berkeley cardinal}”.
$$

This predicts a specific inner model of determinacy and regular $\Theta$ has the stated Berkeley-cardinal property at $\omega_1$. No resolution is supplied in the source context.
technical_review: Full scope is a uniform inner-model assertion over all relevant M and club-many critical points. A finite witness or consistency example cannot settle it; requires determinacy, HOD and elementary-embedding infrastructure, beyond bounded screening.
title: Solovay-sequence conjecture on club HOD-Berkeley cardinals

quantifier_scope_review: For every node and every pair of partial colorings, equality of CF on all nine-set tuples implies one global color permutation matching CL on all tuples.
source_body_coverage: No primary body read; literal corpus statement screening only
statement_utf8:
Let $G_i'$ be the graph associated with a node $X_i$ of the smooth tree-decomposition, and let $f$ and $g$ be partial colorings of $G_i'$. For each tuple $\big( A^{(j)} \big)_{1 \le j \le 9}$ in $\mathcal{S}(X_i)$, let $CF_f\left(\big( A^{(j)} \big)_{1 \le j \le 9}\right)$ denote the number of color classes represented by the tuple, and let $CL_f\left(\big( A^{(j)} \big)_{1 \le j \le 9}\right)$ denote its color class function. **Color class count function equivalence conjecture.** If $f$ and $g$ have the same color class count function, namely

$$
CF_f\left(\big( A^{(j)} \big)_{1 \le j \le 9}\right)=CF_g\left(\big( A^{(j)} \big)_{1 \le j \le 9}\right)
$$

for every $\big( A^{(j)} \big)_{1 \le j \le 9}\in\mathcal{S}(X_i)$, then there is a permutation $\pi$ of the colors such that

$$
CL_{\pi\circ f}\left(\big( A^{(j)} \big)_{1 \le j \le 9}\right)=CL_g\left(\big( A^{(j)} \big)_{1 \le j\le 9}\right)
$$

for every $\big( A^{(j)} \big)_{1 \le j \le 9}\in\mathcal{S}(X_i)$. The conjecture would allow the algorithm to store color class count functions instead of full color class functions, potentially removing the restriction that the maximum degree $\Delta$ is constant and yielding a polynomial-time algorithm.
technical_review: If tuples partition colors into disjoint fibers, equal fiber sizes give a permutation; overlapping fibers can defeat that implication. The actual S(X_i), CL and CF definitions are absent, so neither mechanism is licensed. Do not call a generic multiset argument a proof.
title: Color class count function equivalence conjecture for partial colorings

quantifier_scope_review: For each N>=2, general points on P1xP2 and every positive bidegree, the displayed negativity test exactly determines first Betti numbers.
source_body_coverage: No primary body read; literal corpus statement screening only
statement_utf8:
Let $N\geq 2$ be an integer, and let $U\subseteq(\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^2)^N$ be a dense open subset. For $(P_1,P_2,\dots,P_N)\in U$, set $X=\{P_1,\dots,P_N\}$, and let $S/I_X$ be its coordinate ring with bigraded Betti numbers $\beta_{1,(i,j)}$. For a matrix $H$ indexed by $(i,j)\in\mathbb Z^2$, write

$$
DH=(\Delta^C)^2(\Delta^R)^3H.
$$

Let $H_X$ be the Hilbert matrix of $X$.

**Weakened Minimal Resolution Conjecture.** The set $X$ has a generic Hilbert matrix as in the source definition, and, for every fixed $(i,j)>(0,0)$, one has $\beta_{1,(i,j)}>0$ if and only if

$$
DH_X(i,j)<0\quad\text{and}\quad DH_X(i',j')\leq 0
$$

for all $(i',j')\leq(i,j)$ with $(i',j')\neq(0,0)$. Whenever this condition holds,

$$
\beta_{1,(i,j)}=-DH_X(i,j).
$$

This is a weakened version of the Minimal Resolution Conjecture for sufficiently general points in $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^2$: it only prescribes the first Betti numbers, but that control is intended to determine enough of the resolution to establish the paper's virtual-resolution results. The parser supplies no evidence that the conjecture has been resolved, so its status remains open.
technical_review: Generic Hilbert matrix, difference operators, field and bidegree order must be sourced. Computing resolutions for small N cannot establish the dense-open assertion uniformly; no full-scope algebraic route identified.
title: Weakened Minimal Resolution Conjecture for points in \(\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^2\)

quantifier_scope_review: For each m,l>=1 there exists a connectivity threshold forcing, through any edge and avoiding m prescribed vertices, an induced cycle with l-connected vertex complement.
source_body_coverage: No primary body read; literal corpus statement screening only
statement_utf8:
Let $m$ and $l$ be positive integers. A graph is **$r$-connected** if it remains connected after deletion of any set of fewer than $r$ vertices. Let $G$ be a graph, let $e$ be an edge of $G$, and let $a_1,\ldots,a_m$ be distinct vertices of $G-V(e)$. A cycle is **induced** if it has no chords in the graph containing it. **Hong–Kang–Yu's conjecture.** There exists a smallest positive integer $g(m,l)$ such that, for every $g(m,l)$-connected graph $G$, there is an induced cycle $C$ in $G-\{a_1,\ldots,a_m\}$ containing $e$ and satisfying

$$
G-V(C)
$$

is $l$-connected. Hong, Kang, and Yu posed this as a strengthening of Lovász's conjecture, requiring the cycle to avoid prescribed vertices. The paper's results establish related cases for $l=2$ and $k=1,2$, but do not resolve this general induced-cycle assertion.
technical_review: Inducedness and connected complement must hold simultaneously after all prescribed avoidances. Standard high connectivity gives cycles but not this residual property. The mentioned l=2 cases cannot supply arbitrary l; no bounded obstruction strategy survives arbitrary connectivity.
title: Hong–Kang–Yu induced-cycle conjecture

statement_utf8:
Let $D$ be a group operation table, and let $T$ be the tensor represented by the HyperCube factors. For a finite group, write $\varrho$ for its unitary regular representation, so that the factor slices satisfy

$$
A_g=B_g=C_g^\intercal=\varrho(g).
$$

Let $\mathcal{H}$ denote the HyperCube Regularizer and impose the constraint $T=D$.

**HyperCube regularizer minimizer conjecture.** The unitary group representation $A_g=B_g=C_g^\intercal=\varrho(g)$ describes the unique minimizer of $\mathcal{H}$ up to unitary basis changes, and its minimum regularizer loss is

$$
\mathcal{H}^*(D)=3\lVert D\rVert_F^2.
$$

This conjecture proposes that the regular representation is not only sufficient to reproduce every finite group operation table exactly, but is also the unique optimal solution, modulo unitary changes of basis, for the constrained HyperCube regularization problem.
technical_review: Tensor factor dimensions, real/complex conventions, factor-to-tensor contraction and H are absent. Gauge transformations or extra zero blocks could produce spurious literal counterexamples; need exact source gauge group and admissible sizes before optimization.
title: Uniqueness of the unitary group representation minimizer for HyperCube regularization

quantifier_scope_review: N tends to infinity; row ranks, decreasing limiting membership function, reversal for maxima and distribution universality under fast tails.
source_body_coverage: No primary body read; literal corpus statement screening only
statement_utf8:
Let $\widetilde{J}=(J+J')/2$ be the symmetrized coupling matrix, let $\widetilde{H}$ be the Hamiltonian obtained by replacing $J$ with $\widetilde{J}$, and let $[i]$ denote the index of the $i$-th smallest row sum of $\widetilde{J}$. Thus $\eta^{\min}_{[i]}=1$ and $\eta^{\max}_{[i]}=1$ mean that the corresponding row belongs to the minimizer and maximizer, respectively.

**Limiting row-membership probability conjecture.** As $N\to\infty$,

$$
\mathbb{P}(\eta^{\min}_{[i]}=1)=f_{\min}\left(\frac{[i]}{N}\right)+o(1),
$$

where $f_{\min}$ is decreasing. Similarly,

$$
\mathbb{P}(\eta^{\max}_{[i]}=1)=f_{\max}\left(\frac{[i]}{N}\right)+o(1),
$$

with

$$
f_{\max}\left(\frac{[i]}{N}\right)=f_{\min}\left(1-\frac{[i]}{N}\right).
$$

Moreover, there exists $\lambda_0>0$ such that $f_{\min}(\lambda)=1$ for all $\lambda<\lambda_0$; if the tails of $J_{i,j}$ decay sufficiently fast, the limiting function does not depend on the distribution of $J_{i,j}$.

This conjecture proposes a universal, monotone limiting profile for membership in the minimizer and maximizer when rows are ordered by their row sums. The source gives numerical motivation but no proof or resolution; the maximizer probability line appears to contain a typographical omission in the supplied statement.
technical_review: No distribution/independence law, minimizer tie rule, Hamiltonian or uniformity of the o(1) is specified. Symmetry may give the min/max relation but not convergence, plateau or universality. A finite QUBO simulation would not establish these limits.
title: The limiting row-membership probability conjecture for QUBO minimizers and maximizers

statement_utf8:
Let $\phi:\mathbb{R}^{n-1}\to\mathbb{R}$ be smooth, and let $\mathcal{M}_{\phi}=\{(\xi,\phi(\xi)):\xi\in[0,1]^{n-1}\}$. A set $S\subset[0,1]^{n-1}$ is $(\phi,\delta)$-flat when it satisfies the flatness condition defined in the paper. For a measurable function $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{C}$ and measurable $S$, let $f_S$ denote the Fourier restriction of $f$ to $S\times\mathbb{R}$. **High-dimensional $p$ decoupling conjecture.** For every $\epsilon>0$, there is a sufficiently large $A=A(\epsilon)$ such that, for every $\delta>0$, one can find a finitely overlapping collection $\mathcal{S}_{\delta}$ of subsets of $[0,1]^{n-1}$ satisfying

$$
\sum_{S\in\mathcal{S}_{\delta}}\chi_S\leq C_{\epsilon}\log(\delta^{-1}),
$$

with every $S$ $(\phi,A\delta)$-flat, and such that for $2\leq p\leq\frac{2(n+1)}{n-1}$,

$$
\|f\|_{L^p}\leq C_{\epsilon}\delta^{-\epsilon}(\#\mathcal{S}_{\delta})^{\frac12-\frac1p}\left(\sum_{S\in\mathcal{S}_{\delta}}\|f_S\|_{L^p}^p\right)^{\frac1p}
$$

for all $f$ whose Fourier supports are contained in $N_{\delta}(\mathcal{M}_{\phi})$. This is proposed as a possible extension of $\ell^p$ decoupling to higher dimensions; the statement is conjectural for general smooth $\phi$.
technical_review: Paper-specific flatness and neighborhood conventions are missing. Literal delta>0 makes log(delta^-1) problematic at1; fixing the small-scale domain earns no credit. General smooth hypersurfaces need uniform geometry and multiscale inequalities, not a small certificate.
title: High-dimensional $p$ decoupling conjecture for smooth hypersurfaces

statement_utf8:
A **pair construction** of a $3$-graph coloring is a coloring of $K_N^{(3)}$ obtained from functions $f:\binom{[N]}{2}\to[p]$ and $g:[p]^3\to\{\operatorname{red},\operatorname{blue}\}$ by setting

$$
\chi_{f,g}(\{i,j,k\})=g(f(i,j),f(j,k),f(k,i))
$$

for $i<j<k$. Its complexity is $p$. For $3$-graphs $G,H$, let $r^p(G,H)$ be the smallest $n$ such that every $2$-edge-coloring of $K_n^{(3)}$ of complexity at most $p$ contains a red copy of $G$ or a blue copy of $H$. **Low-complexity encoding conjecture.** There exists an absolute constant $a>0$ such that, for all $3$-graphs $G$ and $H$,

$$
r^p(G,H)\ge r(G,H)^a
$$

whenever $p>r(G,H)^{o(1)}$. This conjecture asks whether Ramsey colorings can retain a polynomial fraction of the unrestricted Ramsey number while using subpolynomial pair-construction complexity. The source gives no resolution.
technical_review: The o(1) condition requires a precise asymptotic quantifier, not a threshold for an isolated pair. Encoding every triple via distinct pair labels uses quadratic complexity and does not settle the asserted subpolynomial regime.
title: Low-complexity encoding conjecture for hypergraph Ramsey colorings

quantifier_scope_review: All m with n>=11 for SLP; all even m and all n for SLP/HRR; all m,n for HLP.
source_body_coverage: No primary body read; literal corpus statement screening only
statement_utf8:
Let $m,n$ be positive integers and define the graded Artinian Gorenstein algebra

$$
A(m,n)=\frac{{\mathbb Q}[e_1,\ldots,e_n]}{(e_1(m),\ldots,e_n(m))}.
$$

If $A(m,n)$ has socle degree $d$, its strong Lefschetz property (SLP) means that there is a linear form $\ell\in A_1$ for which

$$
\times\ell^{d-2i}\colon A_i\longrightarrow A_{d-i},\qquad 0\leq i\leq\left\lfloor\frac d2\right\rfloor,
$$

are all isomorphisms. The Lefschetz property with respect to the Hilbert function (HLP) means that these maps have rank equal to the minimum dimension of the graded components between $i$ and $d-i$. The complex Hodge–Riemann relations (complex HRR) mean that these maps have signature equal to the alternating sum of the even first differences of the Hilbert function.

**Almkvist–Lefschetz strengthening.** (i) For each $m$, the algebra $A(m,n)$ satisfies the SLP for all $n\geq 11$. (ii) Moreover, if $m$ is even, then $A(m,n)$ satisfies the SLP for all $n$. (iii) For each $m$, the algebra $A(m,n)$ satisfies HLP for all $n$. (iv) If $m$ is even, then $A(m,n)$ satisfies the complex HRR.

SLP implies unimodality of the Hilbert function, so the first two assertions strengthen Almkvist's conjecture; the latter assertions concern finer Lefschetz and signature properties. The source states that items (i)–(iii) were posed in earlier work and item (iv) is new, but gives no resolution of these assertions.
technical_review: The polynomials e_i(m) and grading are not supplied. Hilbert-function unimodality is necessary but does not prove multiplication-map ranks or signatures. Small symbolic matrices would be parameter helpers only.
title: The Lefschetz and Hodge–Riemann strengthening of Almkvist's conjecture

quantifier_scope_review: For random G_n,delta and the specified algorithm, the output label interval is almost uniformly distributed within [0,1].
source_body_coverage: No primary body read; literal corpus statement screening only
statement_utf8:
Let $G_{n,\delta}$ be an Erdős–Rényi random graph, and construct a temporal instance ${\cal I}(G_{n,\delta})$ by assigning labels to the edges of $G_{n,\delta}$ independently and uniformly at random in $[0,\delta]$, and assigning labels to all other edges independently and uniformly at random in $[\delta,1]$. For a vertex set $Q$, define its label interval by

$$
\Delta(Q)=\left[\min(\lambda(e):e\in Q),\max(\lambda(e):e\in Q)\right].
$$

Let $Q^*$ be the $\delta$-clique constructed by algorithm ${\cal A}_{SRT}$ on instance ${\cal I}(G_{n,\delta})$. **Uniform-distribution conjecture.** Then $\Delta(Q^*)$ is distributed almost uniformly at random within $[0,1]$. This conjecture concerns the distribution of the interval containing the labels of an algorithmically found temporal clique and is proposed as a possible route toward proving the reduction from temporal-clique approximation to maximum-clique approximation in Erdős–Rényi graphs; no proof or resolution is given.
technical_review: Algorithm A_SRT, delta-clique, limiting regime and metric on interval distributions are missing. Shifting edge labels is not measure-preserving because the two label populations have different conditional laws; no symmetry shortcut justified.
title: The uniform-distribution conjecture for temporal-clique label intervals

quantifier_scope_review: Every length n, maximizing quaternary residue a and corresponding binary residue a'; source fixed phi9 maps the whole class bijectively.

statement_utf8:
Let $H(n,q,s,a)$ denote a Helberg code with length $n$, alphabet size $q$, deletion parameter $s$, and residue $a$. Let $a$ be the residue corresponding to the maximum number of codewords in $H(n,4,1,a)$, and let $a'$ be the corresponding binary-code residue. **Naisargik mapping conjecture.** There is a one-to-one mapping $\phi$ between the codewords of $H(n,4,1,a)$ and $H(2n,2,2,a')$ such that, for every codeword $c\in H(n,4,1,a)$, $\phi(c)\in H(2n,2,2,a')$, and

$$
\phi(H(n,4,1,a))=H(2n,2,2,a').
$$

Thus all codewords of the Naisargik image satisfy $\phi(H(n,4,1,a))\subseteq H(2n,2,2,a')$. The mapping is used in the paper's argument relating deletion correction in quaternary Helberg codes to correction in their binary Naisargik images; the supplied text gives no independent resolution evidence for this assertion.
technical_review: Read primary Definition3, TableI and Conjecture2 plus its proof paragraph. That paragraph is finite data, not proof. Exhaustive n=1..7 verifies every maximizing residue maps onto a single full binary class; no general recurrence bridge or novelty clearance. Source also proves error-correction properties, which do not prove residue-class equality. No proposal.
title: The Naisargik mapping between quaternary and binary Helberg codes

quantifier_scope_review: Every type-A Bruhat interval and amazing upper hypercube decomposition z satisfies the full R-polynomial expansion.
source_body_coverage: No primary body read; literal corpus statement screening only
statement_utf8:
Let $W$ be a Coxeter group of type $A$, and let $u,v\in W$ with $u\leq v$. An upper hypercube decomposition $z\in [u,v]$ is called **amazing** when, for every $x\in [u,v]$, the intersection $[z,v]\cap[x,v]$ has a minimum $z\vee x$, and this minimum is a hypercube decomposition of $[x,v]$. Write $W^z_{[u,v]}$ for the associated set of elements used in the $R$-element expansion, and let $\widetilde{R}_{u,v}$ denote the Kazhdan–Lusztig $\widetilde{R}$-polynomial.

**Amazing-hypercube $R$-element conjecture.** The element $z$ is an $R$-element, meaning that

$$
\widetilde{R}_{u,v}=\sum_{p\in W^z_{[u,v]}}q^{\operatorname{d}(u,p)}\widetilde{R}_{p,v}.
$$

This is presented as a weak version of a conjecture from Brenti and Marietti, which had been verified up to $W=S_6$. The assertion is intended to provide a combinatorial route toward the Kazhdan–Lusztig combinatorial invariance conjecture.

Let $A=\bigwedge^2\mathbb{C}^{N+1}$ denote the space of skew-symmetric matrices. **Irreducible-component conjecture.** For every $r\in[N+1]$: (i) $\mathcal{SC}_1=S=S^2\mathbb{C}^{N+1}$ is an irreducible component of $\mathcal{SC}_r$; (ii) $(X_{n-r})_{S_{n-r}}^\vee$ is an irreducible component of $\mathcal{SC}_r$ for every $2\le r\le N+1$; and (iii) $A=\bigwedge^2\mathbb{C}^{N+1}$ is an irreducible component of $\mathcal{SC}_r$ for all $N\ge 3$ and even $r\in[N]$. The conjecture is motivated by symbolic computations for $N=2$ and $N=3$, which exhibit several of these components, while the preceding example also shows that the varieties $\mathcal{SC}_i$ need not be nested. Determining all irreducible components in general remains open.

title: Conjecture on irreducible components of varieties with symmetric compound matrices

$$

for every choice of coefficients, where $\Theta=\{\varphi_1,\ldots,\varphi_N\}$. **The $l^p$ restriction conjecture.** There exists a subset $\Psi\subset\Phi$ satisfying

$$
K_p^*(\Psi)\lesssim 1\quad\text{and}\quad |\Psi|\sim K_q^*(\Phi)^{-2q/p}|\Phi|^{q/p}.

An **iterated blowup of an edge** is a complete tripartite 3-graph, or a 3-graph formed by repeatedly placing another iterated blowup in one or more parts; a 3-graph is **iterated tripartite** when it is contained in such a blowup.

**The iterated-tripartite classification conjecture.** For a 3-graph $H$, there exists a constant $c$ depending only on $H$ such that

$$
r(H,K_n^{(3)})\leq n^c
$$

for all $n$ if and only if $H$ is a subgraph of an iterated blowup of an edge.

technical_review: Polynomial sufficiency is explicitly known. Surviving converse requires superpolynomial lower constructions for every excluded H, not just one obstruction. No bounded parameter computation establishes the dichotomy.
title: The iterated-tripartite classification conjecture for off-diagonal 3-graph Ramsey numbers

statement_utf8:

$$
\frac{v(F)!}{|\operatorname{Aut}(F)|}p^{e(F)}\geq 1
$$

for every $F\subseteq G$. A **threshold function** for a sequence of graphs $\{G_n\}$ is a function ${\rm th}(G_n)$ such that, for the random graph $G(n,p(n))$, the appearance probability tends to one when $p(n)/{\rm th}(G_n)\to\infty$ and tends to zero when $p(n)/{\rm th}(G_n)\to 0$. **Kahn–Kalai threshold conjecture.** There is a universal constant $K$ such that, for every sequence $\{G_n\}$, a threshold function for the appearance of $\{G_n\}$ in $G(n,p)$ is at most

$$
p_E(G_n)\log |v(G_n)|.
$$

This conjecture proposes that the first-moment obstruction determines thresholds up to a logarithmic factor, uniformly over all graph sequences. It was proposed by Kahn and Kalai; the supplied text gives no resolution status.
technical_review: Literal p_E uses v(F)! rather than an n-dependent embedding count and displays no K in its bound despite declaring K. Exact graph-threshold formulation must be restored. title: Kahn–Kalai threshold conjecture for graph appearances

statement_utf8:
Let $r\ge 3$ and $1 \le s_1 \le \cdots \le s_r$ be integers, and let $m\coloneqq s_1+\cdots+s_r$. A spanning subgraph $F$ of $K_{s_1,\ldots,s_r}^{r}$ is **rigid** if, for some such integers with $v(F)=s_1+\cdots+s_r$, it satisfies $\tau_i(F)=s_1+\cdots+s_i$ for every $i\in [r-1]$, where $\tau_i(F)$ is the minimum size of a vertex set meeting every edge of $F$ in at least $i$ vertices. For integers $n\ge r$ and $1\le i\le r$, let $G_{n,i,\beta}(s_1,\ldots,s_r)$ be the $n$-vertex $r$-graph whose edges are the $r$-sets meeting a distinguished set of size $\lfloor\beta(s_1+\cdots+s_i)n\rfloor-1$ in at least $i$ vertices. **Revised tiling conjecture.** For every real number $\beta\in\left(0,\frac{1}{m}\right)$, 

$$
\mathrm{ex}(n,\beta n \cdot F)=\max\left\\{|G_{n,i,\beta}(s_1,\ldots,s_r)|\colon i\in [r]\right\\}+o(n^r).
$$

The revision excludes the previously refuted formulation by imposing rigidity, a condition satisfied by complete multipartite hypergraphs and intended to capture the relevant covering-number obstructions. The source does not state a resolution.
technical_review: Rigidity is the extra hypothesis repairing a refuted prior version. Cover-number barriers give lower bounds; a matching upper bound across all rigid F needs a structural tiling theorem. Rounding beta n is a convention only; old nonrigid examples do not apply.
title: Revised asymptotic tiling conjecture for rigid spanning hypergraphs
